_comment: Claude Code takes a deny array directly, which Cursor's IDE agent does not — see ADR-012.
These entries are coarser than the regexes in aios/config.yml because this matcher is
prefix-based: it cannot express 'rm with both -r and -f' or 'curl piped into sh', so each
such rule widens to the base command. Wider is the safe direction for a deny list.
That is why M2-03 maps this list rather than translating it: there is no lossless
conversion, and pretending there is would produce entries that silently match nothing.
Everything below permissions.deny is GENERATED by .github/scripts/generate-deny-lists.py
from aios/config.yml. Edit the config and regenerate; an edit made here is overwritten,
and CI fails while the two disagree. Each coarse prefix is declared in the config beside
the regex it widens, so a new regex with no declared prefix fails rather than quietly
existing in one tool and not the other.
The regexes themselves also run here, as the Bash preToolUse hook — the deny array is the
prefix-matched floor and the hook is the precise layer, the same one Cursor gets.
This layer is Advisory. Server-side required review is what contains the agent.
The hooks below point at aios/bin/hooks/, the same scripts Cursor's .cursor/hooks.json
registers. That is the whole of M4-07: one implementation, two registration lines, so the
drift surface is the pointer rather than the logic. Two copies of a mode permission set
drift against each other and the one nobody is looking at goes stale.
UNVERIFIED, deliberately and visibly. Claude Code is not installed here (ADR-009), so
neither the event shape nor the response contract below has been measured — they are
written to the documentation. That is the exact thing that caused the M2-08 outage, and
the reason it is acceptable here and was not there is the failure mode: these deny via
exit code 2, so a wrong guess means the control does not fire, not that every command is
refused. Shipping nothing would leave the first person with Claude Code installed with no
control at all. M4-13 measures it and this comment comes out.
Cursor was measured to ignore exit code 2 despite documenting it as blocking, which is
why respond.py branches on the caller instead of using one mechanism for both.
